title: Prospective Associations Between Older Adults’ Social Connections and Trajectories of Change in Physical Activity and Psychological Well-Being During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Parallel Process Approach
abstract: Associations between seven social connection trajectories and changes in physical activity (PA) and psychological well-being were examined among older adults ( N = 890, M age = 65.05 years, SD = 6.91) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Six online monthly surveys were administered between October 2021 and May 2022. Latent growth curve modeling demonstrated injunctive and descriptive norms did not change over time. Social network, relatedness, stress, and negative affect decreased, and social support quantity and quality increased over time. Social participation, positive affect, and light-intensity PA changed quadratically, and moderate to vigorous PA increased steadily and then slowed over time. Changes in social participation, social network, and social support were positively associated with changes in moderate to vigorous PA and psychological well-being. Findings support theories suggesting social connections play a dynamic, multidimensional role in health behaviors and highlight the need for future research examining how social connections contribute to higher intensity PA and well-being among older adults.
